A lot of my stuff can be tricky, but I have confidence that you can nail this recipe for Chicken Cordon Bleu. It has a french name, so it sounds intimidating, but don't worry, I know you can do it.

Hardware:

Plastic wrap, meat hammer, wide saute pan, tongs, three mixing bowls, and an oven.

Software:

4 Boneless Chicken Breasts, fat trimmed

Grated cheese, dealer's choice (see below)

Fresh Black Forest Ham (tradition calls for prociutto, but if you don't want to spring for it, BF ham works just as fine).

(I should also point out that I don't really measure things, so the actual totals are a bit of guesswork)

2C AP flour

4-6 eggs

3 1/2 C Panko bread crumbs

Salt and pepper, to taste

Olive oil

With the cheese, it really is up to you. Tradition calls for gruyere, which I absolutely cannot stand. I'll pick different kinds on different days, but you certainly will want something a little stiffer than American, that shit is bland as hell anyway. Stay clear of things that are soft as, say, provolone. Something in the Swiss area of firmness or harder should do.

I, personally go for a mix of Jack and Muenster.

Now, the fun part. First, pre-heat your oven to 350°. Put down a layer of plastic wrap, and sprinkle it with water. Put down one chicken breast, sprinkle with water, and put a layer of plastic down on top. I usually cut them about 18 inches long. The water, if you're wondering, is to prevent sticking. Gently pound the breast to about 1/4 inch thickness. Set aside and repeat with the remaining three breasts. With that finished, layer each chicken breast with a slice of the ham (2 if thin,) and a layer of your cheese. Next, fold up the wide sides of your chicken, and roll them up like you're making a little burrito. With the open-side down, give each a little press just to help close them up.

In your first bowl, add your flour, eggs to the second, and bread crumbs to the third. What you're doing here is called "standard breading procedure." Beat the eggs thoroughly, and add enough milk to make it a creamy yellow. Something close to this:

http://www.color-hex.com/color/ffffcc

I had a chef ask me once, which of these three bowls do you season? I answered "why not all three?" He agreed. Mix your salt and pepper into each bowl.

Coat your chicken rolls in the flour, shake off the excess. Coat it in the egg wash, then coat it in the bread crumbs. Wet things and dry things stick together, so the science is the dry flour sticks to the wet chicken, the eggs to the flour, and the bread crumbs to the eggs. I don't deviate from tradition on this one. Repeat with remaining three breasts.

Over medium-high heat, brown your chicken rolls in your large saute pan with just enough oil to coat the bottom of the pan. Start with the open-side down. Brown all sides of the chicken then put them in the oven. Roast in the oven for 10-15 minutes, I'd say. Til they're done, lol.

Conceivably, you could skip the sauté step altogether and roast them for about 20-25 open side down, until golden brown and cooked through.

This is a classic recipe that is sure to impress your friends. It takes maybe an hour start to finish.

Cut onions in a pot with olive oil, roast them, add mincemeat, roast until meat is done, add sieved tomatoes and tomatoe paste.
